en: If you stir up the camp thoroughly,
You will see your champion,
The sign is the model of the word,
It cannot be found by one who understands speech,
In short, the famed Joytoy,
Another’s enemy from here,
Another has none, his hand cannot reach,
If you face the enemy apart from the others,
See the warrior’s secret as support,
If you are numerous, if you are a song,
If you are a hero when united,
Will it not fall into the hands at the mound,
If you are a diverse people who have prospered,
Will the enemy not disturb the heart,
If you are divided, you are violent,
With the men, we shall not be broken,
And drove them into anxious thought
From that day it was thus
Keeping watch in that manner
If a head were cut off, all the people would know
He was cowed and frightened by this
Those two khans of Karagul
Settled themselves at Belen’s ridge
One guarded the pass
A heart of iron, a steadfast heart
He would not yield easily to an enemy
For the sake of those men
A legacy remained afterward
To the people, Kozoy and the two clans
They seized and took the livestock
They became masters of the divided herds
Spilling blood in the deep mountains
They joined it to Turdungko
This victory was Ak Jолтой’s
Regard it as the fruit of your great strength
Your elder gathered the inheritance
Strike the black host in this place
Those two heroes of Kozoy
All fell into the struggle
The two chargers did not break
From the place where they stood
He firmly cast down the white pavilion
You stand there in great commotion
You are an immovable iron body
Tell me, what road leads to the seat of honor
My rear will not fail or break
Even if a thousand of every thousand come
You have broken those whose saddles never slipped
I will hear the word behind you
I am of the two children
Kozoy and Jолтой from here
Our land knows the prepared place
Our land will not be ruined
Leaving the ford, seeking the land
Searching this way with resolve
Taking Kökötöy at the front
What came from the three valleys
You drove them onto the ridge and struck them
With a shout you split the enemy
The son of the land he encountered
Was he truly equal to the hero
You gave support along the road
You struck all the golden host
You set right all that had gone astray
Laying a hand upon the horse’s mane
You darkened them all like coal
You cut through every forelock
Lamenting in grief
You struck all their horses
Was this alone what you had taken
Do not surrender your rear to the ground
The open steppe gave me its power
You should side with Kozoy
Hearing word from your caravan man
Having been born into this world
Hearing that Kenen had come
Coming to my father Kongur
Moving as an ally
If death comes, without hesitation
As though gathering up one’s life
Sharing one purpose together
Our lives together through the world’s turmoil
He joined their midst
Following the road through harsh words
I am the one who kept the treasury moving
When you saw him, you received him
It was for that very month
Created by the one God
The rest were merely kin
To wise and generous Kenen
Your in-laws became enemies
In the fierce battle of destruction
However far they might pursue
This alone was what remained
Ebegey and Kozoy, the two friends
Set him on the road so he may understand
What remained after entering the people
Ebegey spoke again
I am called Ebegey
The pale stallion that never tires
You travel abreast across the broad land
To your formidable father Kenen
From now on I shall stand watching
If you enter among the enemy
I asked what they had left unsaid
To dear lord Kenen
I am fierce when defending the homeland
If Kenen receives him
You will go out against the enemy at the front
Turning the steel blade
If the day is won, he will not part
You gathered the true words
Ebegey rose the next day
Of black Kongur with the blue mane
Come, Kozoy, rise now
Ebegey and Kozoy together
The whole age stood astonished
When the father came forth
He laid out the place of honor
Finding no enemy at the camp
Shall we leave him with his bedding
A hero’s heart and a warrior’s courage
Let no living soul overtake you
We bound our cause to the world
Setting the bull beneath the standard
A pale enemy lies beyond ruined Kongur
Listen thoughtfully, our collective farm,
Going about without sleeping,
From there, Kyrgyz and [?] Kazakh:
Its crescent-shaped ear like a shield,
Its foremost eye like the morning star,
Like a lamb’s tail curled up,
When seen, appearing like this,
Tall, with broad shoulders,
Of medium height, with a stern face,
At the time when stone would burn,
Then a man named Kayyp,
Spoke one word worth ten men’s words,
He spoke stern words to his face,
“If you ask about me,
I myself am of the name Shay,
Of the khoja called Sebet,
The son called Er Jolbors,
Firewood and a crossing [?],
Your people in Kozoy-Joo,
Known as Muslims,
His occupation is worldly trade,
Now before the eyes, now out of sight,
Know it for the sake of your father,
Even if it is a seven-day journey,
If you are wise, understand it,
Born from [?],
Having heard tidings upon tidings,
Climbing across the breadth of the land,
Standing outside and lingering,
Everyone heard of your deeds,
That blooded he-goat [?],
From abundance comes generosity,
Whatever has eyes gnaws at it.
Gnawing at this, it makes it its work,
Let it gnaw however much it thrives,
It does [?] to the four enclosures,
Beginning at the precipice, it takes life,
The blood of us all flows,
Your eye lets this fall to the ground,
In a foreign land it cannot turn aside,
Among foreign people it does no different deed,
Pass from the rich man to true blood,
What sort of man will be strong,
The hardship encountered will be a fire,
Seeing those things,
Did you send it from here to [?],
Without diminishing his people [?],
Did you leave after saddling Burak,
Kenen, who came through the dark night,
Asking my news, his every affair,
Black on the outside, blue at the breast,
There is no hero standing without you,
Train yourself in speech,
Bride, enter among the people,
It is a hero’s deed to wage battle,
Make camp at the Talas citadel,
His mother raced Kozoy’s horse,
Give Kenen the pacing horse,
Saying he should guard the people without losing them,
His anger was like wheat on black earth,
Saying, “Be spent for your people,”
When told to take a cap, he cut off a head,
When told to take boots, his head [?],
Leave that to Kenen,
In awe, defer to him,
It was a land endowed with fortune.
That man’s lineage is from God,
Like the livestock of the abyss,
If you understand, he will act on you quickly,
He will turn what you see into livestock,
If you bring it, he will do it quickly,
Whatever you await, that is the brave man,
That is the unexpectedly formidable man,
Has the scout gone ahead?
Did your mother descend to the place of honor, khan?
The khan has come to Ay-Salam,
Go out once on patrol at night.
My fierce warrior-khan, Tülüş,
My Kara-Kyrgyz, you have your standing,
If you settle after telling Keneş,
He has done the deed he laughed about,
What was lacking was found,
He brought Kök Keneş into contact,
You became my eyes in the enclosure,
My Talas man, mount up,
If you are still traveling,
My word is counsel and advice,
Old man, that is what I said.
Tie him in the enclosure and lead him out,
I speak words reckoned among tens of thousands,
I speak of my concern to Keneş,
May you never disappear from sight.
My cherished khan Keneş,
Searching as he went, he found him,
What sort of swift steed he was,
He proved to be an ambling horse,
A great encampment for the heroes
Baibaba’s great encampment,
To lay down what was advancing,
To Keneş, who captured horses,
If we are not found for the champion.
If you accept it, O world,
Place the blaze before his eyes,
Kanykei spoke smoothly,
Let us be companions on the journey,
To consent to what she said:
“I am exhausted in mind, my companion,
To become a companion,
Being a warrior from the two Tülük,
Ertai, Kozum, and Keneş,
Give your support at Ay-Salam,
“My eyes burn; give it,” she said,
To send my companion among the people,
The warrior Keneş, against the Kalmyks,
To take him as a companion,”—
Thus Eleseñ spoke.
Keneş had cried out without doing it,
His character seems difficult,
He kept speaking amid hardship.
Then Kontoi, dear Kanek,
A word meant for the cherished elder,
Ertai, Kozum, O friends,
The word that you and your people witnessed,
He pondered without making a commotion,
Running a rope toward the ready one,
He was not greatly satisfied by the heedless one,
He pressed it onto the neck and loaded it,
Eleseñ, Kozum—that is the warrior.
He vanished into the mists
Ebegey and Kozoy, those two heroes
